newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes lower on CBOT soybean setback.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes lower on CBOT soybean setback.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed lower after a late sell-off triggered by weakness in CBOT soybeans, floor sources said.
"Weakness in Chicago undermined our prices," one WCE oilseed trader said.
Hedge-related selling also contributed to the decline.

Dealers noted reports that overnight export sales to Japan totalled around 5,000 to 6,000 tonnes. "They (canola exports) are steadily picking up but they (buyers) are not rushing to the trough," one trader said. There was some concern, however, that a strong Canadian dollar could dampen export prospects.
Flaxseed futures closed mixed, with nearbys strengthened by talk of a modest increase in export demand. "Our prices are fairly competitive overseas now," one trade said.
Western barley futures closed higher with commission house buying of July noted. Commercial selling pressure was also reported to be very light. July ended up $0.20 at $141.10.
July feed wheat closed off $1.70 at $168.50.
October feed peas ended off US$0.50 at US$201.00 with July oats finishing unchanged at US$122.00.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
